newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian journalist stabbed, seriously injured.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian journalist stabbed, seriously injured.

text.p: A Cambodian journalist was stabbed and seriously injured in front of his newspaper office by a gang of young people on Wednesday morning, police and officials said.

Kry Sothy, 23, a reporter for the Public Opinion newspaper, was undergoing surgery for a stab wound to the stomach, said Chum Kanal, president of the Khmer Journalists Association, and Chief of Criminal Police Mak Chito.
Mak Chito said the attack had followed an argument between a group of 10 students and Kry Sothy. One student then pulled out a knife and stabbed the reporter once in the abdomen, he said.
Chum Kanal said he did not know whether the incident was politically motivated, but said newspaper staff at that paper and others had recently received threats.
He described Public Opinion as a neutral newspaper.
"We don't know yet about whether there were political motives," Mak Chito told Reuters.
The attack marks the 10th incident against journalists in three years and follows a plea earlier this week by King Norodom Sihanouk for protection of journalists in Cambodia.

Chum Kanal had recently appealed to the king to safeguard journalists, and Thomas Hammarberg, special representative of the U.N. Secretary-General for Human Rights in Cambodia, has expressed concern that acts of violence against journalists, including four deaths, have not been sufficiently investigated.
